comparison.objective: Bimanually cut three specified hedge shoots with shears while preserving flowers, then park the tool; candidate tunes and locks an axis shock absorber.
comparison.physical_skill: Shears task tests two-handle coordination, opening and closing blades around targets, spatially selective cutting, hazard avoidance, and tool return. Candidate tests hex-key engagement, counterholding, fine collar adjustment, setscrew locking, guarded actuation, and repeated response-based tuning.
comparison.success_condition: Shears success requires three cuts within 1.8 cm of target height, no flower cut, closed tool placement, and arm return. Candidate requires two safe ≥0.85 J cycles with ≤12 mm travel and lock retention. Candidate omits numeric rebound, overload, drift, and locking-torque thresholds.
comparison.reason: Selective bimanual cutting and avoidance of protected stems do not test adjustment calibration or post-lock behavior under impacts; shared bimanual coordination alone is not overlap.
